accepted.s:
With reference to the qualifications prescribed for appointment as the Attorney General for India, consider the following statements:
1. The person must be a citizen of India.
2. The person must have been a Judge of a High Court for at least five years, or an advocate of a High Court for at least ten years.
3. An eminent jurist may also be appointed if the President considers the person suitable.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Article 76 requires the Attorney General to satisfy the qualifications for appointment as a Supreme Court Judge, including the stated judicial, advocacy or eminent-jurist qualifications.
accepted.tq: Combine the constitutional qualification routes and check whether the broader category of eminent jurist is included.
accepted.sec: Attorney General - Article 76, appointment, qualification, term, removal

accepted.s: In relation to the resignation of the Attorney General for India, which one of the following is correct?
o: The resignation is addressed to the President
The resignation is addressed to the Union Law Minister
The resignation is addressed to the Chief Justice of India
The resignation is addressed to the Prime Minister
accepted.x: The Attorney General resigns by addressing the resignation to the President.
accepted.tq: Use the appointing authority and the resignation authority as a paired constitutional relationship.
accepted.sec: Attorney General - Article 76, appointment, qualification, term, removal

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the removal of the Attorney General for India is correct?
o: Removal can be ordered only by the Supreme Court
Removal requires impeachment by both Houses of Parliament
The Constitution specifies detailed grounds and a special removal procedure
The Constitution does not specify grounds or a separate removal procedure; the office is held during the President's pleasure
accepted.x: The Constitution does not prescribe specific grounds or a special procedure for removal of the Attorney General. The office is held during the pleasure of the President.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an office held during pleasure from constitutional offices having a prescribed removal procedure.
accepted.sec: Attorney General - Article 76, appointment, qualification, term, removal

accepted.s: The convention that the Attorney General resigns when the Council of Ministers resigns or is replaced is primarily related to the fact that the Attorney General is appointed on the advice of the:
accepted.x: The Attorney General is appointed by the President on the advice of the Council of Ministers. By convention, the Attorney General resigns when that Council resigns or is replaced.
accepted.tq: Link the convention to the political advice underlying the appointment rather than to the formal appointing authority alone.
accepted.sec: Attorney General - Article 76, appointment, qualification, term, removal

accepted.s: Who determines the remuneration of the Attorney General for India?
accepted.x: The remuneration of the Attorney General is determined by the President.
accepted.tq: Apply the authority-power test: identify which constitutional authority is assigned the remuneration decision.
accepted.sec: Attorney General - Article 76, appointment, qualification, term, removal

accepted.s: The Attorney General is consulted through the Ministry of Law primarily on:
o: All administrative matters of the Union Government
accepted.x: References to the Attorney General are made through the Ministry of Law, and consultation is confined to legal matters of real importance.
accepted.tq: Watch for the overbroad word 'all' and identify the carefully limited scope of consultation.
accepted.sec: Highest law officer of India

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Attorney General — Statutory office; Solicitor General — Constitutional office
Attorney General — Constitutional office under Article 76; Solicitor General — Statutory office
Attorney General — Judicial office under Article 124; Solicitor General — Constitutional office under Article 165
Attorney General — Parliamentary office; Solicitor General — Judicial office
accepted.x: The Attorney General is a constitutional authority under Article 76, whereas the Solicitor General is a statutory office.
accepted.tq: Separate constitutional and statutory offices before comparing their functions.
accepted.sec: Highest law officer of India

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements best distinguishes the Solicitor General from the Attorney General?
o: The Solicitor General advises State Governments while the Attorney General advises only courts
The Solicitor General assists the Attorney General and is confined to appearing in courts for the Union
The Solicitor General is the first law officer and the Attorney General is the second law officer
The Solicitor General is the head of the judiciary and the Attorney General assists him
accepted.x: The Solicitor General is the second law officer, assists the Attorney General and is confined to appearing in courts for the Union; the Attorney General is the chief legal adviser to the Government of India.
accepted.tq: Compare the offices by rank, advisory role and court-related function rather than by title alone.
accepted.sec: Highest law officer of India

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Chief Justice of India is the head of the judiciary.
2. The Attorney General is a government law officer and the chief legal adviser to the Government of India.
3. The Solicitor General is the second law officer of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Chief Justice of India heads the judiciary, while the Attorney General and Solicitor General occupy the first and second positions among Union law officers respectively.
accepted.tq: Keep the head of the judiciary distinct from the hierarchy of government law officers.
accepted.sec: Highest law officer of India

accepted.s: The order of precedence assigned to the Attorney General, Solicitor General, and Advocates General is, respectively:
accepted.x: The Attorney General is placed at 11, the Solicitor General at 23, and the Additional Solicitors General and Advocates General at 25 in the stated order of precedence.
accepted.tq: Read the numerical sequence as an order-of-precedence comparison and avoid reversing the office hierarchy.
accepted.sec: Highest law officer of India

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Solicitor General — Second law officer of India
Chief Justice of India — Government's first law officer
Attorney General — Constitutional office under Article 76
Attorney General — Chief legal adviser to the Government of India
accepted.x: The Chief Justice of India is the head of the judiciary, not the government's first law officer. The Attorney General is the chief legal adviser and first law officer of India.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped institutional role among closely related constitutional and legal offices.
accepted.sec: Highest law officer of India

accepted.s:
With reference to the Advocate General of a State, consider the following statements:
1. The Advocate General is appointed by the Governor.
2. The Advocate General holds office during the pleasure of the Governor.
3. The remuneration of the Advocate General is determined by the Governor.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct under the constitutional arrangement governing the Advocate General of a State.
accepted.tq: Use the State-level parallel of the Attorney General arrangement while retaining the Governor as the relevant authority.
accepted.sec: Advocate General - appointment, duties, Art. 177, remuneration

accepted.s: Under Article 177, the Advocate General of a State may:
o: Speak and take part in the proceedings of either House of the State Legislature and its committees, but not vote
Vote in the State Legislature but not speak in its committees
Dissolve the State Legislature when legal advice is sought
Participate only in the Legislative Assembly and vote in both Houses
accepted.x: Article 177 permits the Advocate General to speak and take part in either House of the State Legislature and its committees, but does not confer a right to vote.
accepted.tq: Separate the right to participate from the right to vote, a standard constitutional distinction.
accepted.sec: Advocate General - appointment, duties, Art. 177, remuneration

accepted.s: Which Article provides that the Advocate General enjoys the privileges of a member of the State Legislature?
accepted.x: Article 194(4) extends legislative privileges to the Advocate General in the State Legislature. Article 105(4) performs the corresponding function for the Attorney General at the Union level.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the participation article from the legislative-privileges article and separate Union from State provisions.
accepted.sec: Advocate General - appointment, duties, Art. 177, remuneration

accepted.s: The right of audience of the Advocate General extends to:
o: Only the High Court of the State
accepted.x: The Advocate General has the right of audience in any court within the State. The Attorney General has the corresponding right of audience in all courts in India.
accepted.tq: Use the territorial scope of the office to distinguish the State law officer from the Union law officer.
accepted.sec: Advocate General - appointment, duties, Art. 177, remuneration

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

a. Attorney General — Article 76
b. Advocate General — Article 165
c. Attorney General's parliamentary rights — Article 88
d. Advocate General's State Legislature rights — Article 177
accepted.x: The correct matching is Attorney General—Article 76, Advocate General—Article 165, Attorney General's parliamentary rights—Article 88, and Advocate General's State Legislature rights—Article 177.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure Article-office pairs and then verify the corresponding legislative-rights provisions.
accepted.sec: State-level counterpart of the Attorney General

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Attorney General and the Advocate General:
1. The Attorney General is qualified to be a Supreme Court Judge, whereas the Advocate General is qualified to be a High Court Judge.
2. The Attorney General holds office during the pleasure of the President, whereas the Advocate General holds office during the pleasure of the Governor.
3. The remuneration of both offices is determined by the President.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false: the Attorney General's remuneration is determined by the President, while the Advocate General's remuneration is determined by the Governor.
accepted.tq: Compare corresponding entries row by row and detect the reversed authority in the remuneration row.
accepted.sec: State-level counterpart of the Attorney General

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Attorneys General of India in chronological order of holding office, beginning with the earliest:
A. K.K. Venugopal
B. M.C. Setalvad
C. Mukul Rohatgi
D. R. Venkataramani
accepted.x: M.C. Setalvad was the first, followed by Mukul Rohatgi, K.K. Venugopal and R. Venkataramani in the sequence represented here.
accepted.tq: Fix the first office-holder and then place the later Attorneys General in sequence.
accepted.sec: Attorneys General of India → FIRST and current

accepted.s: K.K. Venugopal served as the Attorney General of India during which period?
accepted.x: K.K. Venugopal served as Attorney General of India from 2017 to 2022.
accepted.tq: Treat the paired years as a tenure range and distinguish it from the tenures of neighbouring office-holders.
accepted.sec: Attorneys General of India → FIRST and current

accepted.s: Who is the Attorney General of India as stated for September 2026?
accepted.x: R. Venkataramani is the current Attorney General of India as stated for September 2026. He was first appointed in 2022 and was reappointed for a two-year term in 2025.
accepted.tq: Apply the current-affairs date carefully and distinguish the present office-holder from earlier Attorneys General.
accepted.sec: Attorneys General of India → FIRST and current

accepted.s: R. Venkataramani was first appointed as Attorney General of India in:
accepted.x: R. Venkataramani was first appointed Attorney General of India in 2022 and was subsequently reappointed for a two-year term in 2025.
accepted.tq: Separate the first appointment year from the later reappointment year.
accepted.sec: Attorneys General of India → FIRST and current

accepted.s: Under Article 88, the Attorney General may take part in:
o: Only the Lok Sabha and its committees
Either House of Parliament, a joint sitting and committees of which he is named a member
Only the Rajya Sabha and joint sittings
Parliamentary proceedings only after becoming a nominated member
accepted.x: Article 88 permits the Attorney General to speak and take part in either House, joint sittings and committees of which he is named a member. This right does not make him a member of Parliament.
accepted.tq: Read the full scope of participation and avoid converting a right to attend into membership.
accepted.sec: Rights of AG in Parliament - Art. 88; right of audience

accepted.s: Which one of the following rights is NOT available to the Attorney General under Article 88?
o: The right to vote in parliamentary proceedings
The right to take part in a joint sitting of Parliament
The right to speak in either House of Parliament
The right to take part in a committee of which he is named a member
accepted.x: Article 88 permits participation and speaking but does not confer a right to vote. The Attorney General is not a voting member of Parliament by virtue of that Article.
accepted.tq: Find the one power expressly excluded from a broad participation provision.
accepted.sec: Rights of AG in Parliament - Art. 88; right of audience

accepted.s: The parliamentary privileges of the Attorney General are derived from:
accepted.x: Article 105(4) provides the parliamentary privileges applicable to the Attorney General. Article 88 deals with the right to speak and participate without a right to vote.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Article granting participation from the Article extending parliamentary privileges.
accepted.sec: Rights of AG in Parliament - Art. 88; right of audience

accepted.s: Which Article, among the following, specifically deals with the Attorney General's right to speak and participate in Parliament without voting rights?
accepted.x: Article 88 confers the Attorney General's right to speak and take part in parliamentary proceedings without the right to vote. Article 78 concerns the duties of the Prime Minister in relation to the President.
accepted.tq: Reject the look-alike Article number and identify the precise constitutional provision.
accepted.sec: Rights of AG in Parliament - Art. 88; right of audience

accepted.s: Additional Advocates General are appointed primarily to:
o: Replace the Governor in legal matters
Assist the office of the Advocate General
Exercise the voting rights of the Advocate General in the Legislature
Serve as members of the Supreme Court
accepted.x: Additional Advocates General assist the office of the Advocate General in discharging its legal responsibilities.
accepted.tq: Match the supporting office with its assistance function and avoid assigning it the principal office's constitutional powers.
accepted.sec: Advocate General - appointment, duties, Art. 177, remuneration
